canonical_record.label: Inferred Dresser geyserite at three localities
canonical_record.summary: Djokic and colleagues interpret microlaminated siliceous rocks at three Dresser Formation DFc1 localities, approximately 2 km apart, as geyserite.

sources.title: Earliest signs of life on land preserved in ca. 3.5 Ga hot spring deposits

statement: Djokic and colleagues interpret microlaminated siliceous rocks at three Dresser Formation DFc1 localities, approximately 2 km apart, as geyserite.

scope.population: Three sampled DFc1 localities in the Dresser Formation, Pilbara Craton
scope.assumptions: Geological, textural and mineralogical comparisons with modern hot-spring deposits
scope.uncertainty: Interpretation by paper authors, not independent confirmation of biological origin
scope.quantifiers: Three localities separated by approximately 2 km

support.quote: Distinctive microlaminated siliceous rocks observed at three DFc1 localities, ∼2 km apart, are interpreted here as geyserite

canonical_record.label: Dresser siliceous ridges interpreted as sinter terracettes
canonical_record.summary: At Dresser locality 1S, the authors interpret convex siliceous ridges above stratiform geyserite as resembling mid- to distal-apron hot-spring sinter terracettes.

sources.title: Earliest signs of life on land preserved in ca. 3.5 Ga hot spring deposits

statement: At Dresser locality 1S, the authors interpret convex siliceous ridges above stratiform geyserite as resembling mid- to distal-apron hot-spring sinter terracettes.

scope.population: Stratiform geyserite and overlying siliceous ridge unit at Dresser locality 1S
scope.assumptions: Resemblance in primary porosity and microtextures to younger hot-spring terracettes
scope.uncertainty: Analogue-based interpretation, not direct proof of microbial construction
scope.quantifiers: 3 cm thick unit; ridges approximately 1 cm across and under 2 cm high

support.quote: stratiform geyserite is overlain by a 3 cm thick unit composed of siliceous, millimetre-thin laminae that form ∼1 cm diameter, low-amplitude (<2 cm), asymmetrical convex ridges

The convex laminae in cross-section resemble sinter terracettes (smaller-scale subsets within sinter terraces) from the mid- to distal-apron facies of hot springs, displaying the primary porosity and microtextures comparable with more recent, microbially derived examples

canonical_record.label: Dresser barite masses interpreted as fossil hot-spring pools
canonical_record.summary: The authors propose that at least some large Dresser barite masses at hydrothermal vein tips are mineralized remnants of terrestrial hot-spring pools and shallow hydrothermal plumbing.

sources.title: Earliest signs of life on land preserved in ca. 3.5 Ga hot spring deposits

statement: The authors propose that at least some large Dresser barite masses at hydrothermal vein tips are mineralized remnants of terrestrial hot-spring pools and shallow hydrothermal plumbing.

scope.population: Some large barite masses associated with upper hydrothermal feeder veins in DFc1
scope.assumptions: Geometric and stratigraphic association with inferred surface sinter and collapsed sediments
scope.uncertainty: Proposed reinterpretation of at least some masses; no claim applying to all barite occurrences
scope.quantifiers: At least some, not all, masses

support.quote: However, new observations suggest that at least some of these barite masses represent the mineralized remnants of terrestrial hot spring pools and associated shallow subsurface hydrothermal plumbing.

These barite masses occur at the uppermost tips of hydrothermal feeder veins along faults (that is, hydrothermal fluid conduits), and some are found immediately beneath overlying strata with known geyserite and siliceous sinter deposits.

canonical_record.label: Inferred gas-bubble preservation in Dresser microbial EPS
canonical_record.summary: The authors interpret roughly 200 µm circular structures in Dresser geyserite as gas bubbles likely trapped in microbial EPS, while leaving thermal-fluid versus metabolic gas origin unresolved.

sources.title: Earliest signs of life on land preserved in ca. 3.5 Ga hot spring deposits

statement: The authors interpret roughly 200 µm circular structures in Dresser geyserite as gas bubbles likely trapped in microbial EPS, while leaving thermal-fluid versus metabolic gas origin unresolved.

scope.population: Circular to sub-circular inclusions in Dresser columnar–botryoidal inferred geyserite at locality 16N
scope.assumptions: Interpretation from microstructure and analogy to exopolymeric substance (EPS) in hot-spring mats
scope.uncertainty: Both bubble identity and EPS preservation are interpreted; source of gas unresolved
scope.quantifiers: Numerous structures of approximately 200 µm diameter

support.quote: Contained within these horizons are numerous circular to sub-circular structures, ∼200 μm in diameter, filled by microquartz and barite, but lined with fine-grained anatase and internal anatase crystal splays that fan inwards from the margins towards the centre of the structures

Therefore, regardless of whether the Dresser bubbles were derived from degassing of thermal fluids or represent metabolic gas derivatives, preservation likely occurred almost immediately, through entrapment in microbial EPS.

canonical_record.label: Dresser quartz fabric proposed as microbial palisade texture
canonical_record.summary: The authors suggest that bedding-normal quartz crystals in Dresser sinter terracettes are analogous to recrystallized microbial palisade fabric formed by silicified filaments.

sources.title: Earliest signs of life on land preserved in ca. 3.5 Ga hot spring deposits

statement: The authors suggest that bedding-normal quartz crystals in Dresser sinter terracettes are analogous to recrystallized microbial palisade fabric formed by silicified filaments.

scope.population: Selected thin laminae in the Dresser locality 1S sinter-terracette unit
scope.assumptions: Analogy between bedding-normal recrystallized quartz fabric and modern silicified microbial filament textures
scope.uncertainty: Source offers a suggested biogenic analogy, not direct identification of original filaments
scope.quantifiers: Some laminae; crystals described as 230 µm high

support.quote: In addition, within the unit of sinter terracettes, some thin laminae display vertically aligned quartz crystals (230 μm high) that wrap around the curved hinge of the convex ridges

Therefore, these vertically aligned quartz crystals are suggested as analogous to recrystallized microbial palisade fabric formed through silicification of microbial filaments oriented perpendicular to bedding surfaces on mid- to distal-apron hot spring terraces

canonical_record.label: Dresser stromatolitic laminates associated with sinter clasts
canonical_record.summary: At Dresser locality 24S, geyserite rip-up clasts occur among domical and conical stromatolitic laminates; their internal laminae and sediment onlap are described as consistent with microbial origin.

sources.title: Earliest signs of life on land preserved in ca. 3.5 Ga hot spring deposits

statement: At Dresser locality 24S, geyserite rip-up clasts occur among domical and conical stromatolitic laminates; their internal laminae and sediment onlap are described as consistent with microbial origin.

scope.population: Dresser locality 24S stromatolitic laminates interbedded with inferred geyserite rip-up clasts
scope.assumptions: Interpretation of sediment onlap and internal stromatolitic textures
scope.uncertainty: Microbial origin is an interpretation described as consistent with, not uniquely proved by, the structures

support.quote: geyserite rip-up clasts found interbedded with elongate domical and conical stromatolitic laminates
Onlapping by these tuffaceous sediments and the irregular internal laminae with faint palimpsest microfabrics within these stromatolites are consistent with a microbial origin

canonical_record.label: Dresser microfossil-like vesicles interpreted as volcanic glass
canonical_record.summary: A 2018 study interprets spheroidal-to-lenticular Dresser microstructures resembling Archean microfossils as silicified and pyritized vesicular volcanic glass based on size, wall ultrastructure and chemistry.

sources.title: Volcanogenic Pseudo-Fossils from the ∼3.48 Ga Dresser Formation, Pilbara, Western Australia

statement: A 2018 study interprets spheroidal-to-lenticular Dresser microstructures resembling Archean microfossils as silicified and pyritized vesicular volcanic glass based on size, wall ultrastructure and chemistry.

scope.population: The microstructure suite examined in the sampled Dresser Formation material
scope.assumptions: Correlative microscopy and comparisons of size distributions, wall ultrastructure and chemistry
scope.uncertainty: Abiogenic interpretation of these samples only; does not reclassify other Archean structures
scope.quantifiers: Studied suite, not all putative Archean microfossils

support.quote: Here, we describe a new suite of spheroidal to lenticular microstructures that morphologically resemble some previously reported Archean microfossils.

Correlative microscopy shows that these objects have a size distribution, wall ultrastructure, and chemistry that are incompatible with a microfossil origin and instead are interpreted as pyritized and silicified fragments of vesicular volcanic glass.

canonical_record.label: Kerogenous carbon associated with Dresser volcanic vesicles
canonical_record.summary: In the studied Dresser volcanic-glass microstructures, organic kerogenous material accompanies altered glass, with some vesicles lined or filled by carbon and organic-rich laminae enveloping multiple vesicles.

sources.title: Volcanogenic Pseudo-Fossils from the ∼3.48 Ga Dresser Formation, Pilbara, Western Australia

statement: In the studied Dresser volcanic-glass microstructures, organic kerogenous material accompanies altered glass, with some vesicles lined or filled by carbon and organic-rich laminae enveloping multiple vesicles.

scope.population: Volcanic-glass microstructures in the sampled Dresser Formation thin sections
scope.assumptions: Reported kerogen association in correlative microscopy observations
scope.uncertainty: Association does not establish biological origin of the vesicles or the carbon
scope.quantifiers: Much of altered glass; some individual vesicles; multiple vesicles within some laminae

support.quote: Organic kerogenous material is associated with much of the altered volcanic glass; variable quantities of organic carbon line or fill the insides of some individual vesicles, while relatively large, tufted organic-rich laminae envelop multiple vesicles.

canonical_record.label: Isolated volcanic vesicles can imitate microfossils
canonical_record.summary: The Dresser pseudo-fossil study cautions that isolated reworked silicified volcanic vesicles can adsorb carbon and become pyritized, complicating early-life identification; nanoscale wall analysis may be required to exclude biogenicity.

sources.title: Volcanogenic Pseudo-Fossils from the ∼3.48 Ga Dresser Formation, Pilbara, Western Australia

statement: The Dresser pseudo-fossil study cautions that isolated reworked silicified volcanic vesicles can adsorb carbon and become pyritized, complicating early-life identification; nanoscale wall analysis may be required to exclude biogenicity.

scope.population: Hypothetical reworked or isolated microstructures of the same type as studied Dresser vesicular glass
scope.assumptions: Extrapolation from alteration and morphology of studied volcanic-glass microstructures
scope.uncertainty: Conditional methodological warning; no claim that all isolated candidate microfossils are abiotic
scope.quantifiers: May prove problematic; nanoscale inspection conditional on such cases

support.quote: However, reworked, isolated, and silicified microstructures of this type may prove particularly problematic in early or extraterrestrial life studies since they adsorb carbon onto their surfaces and are readily pyritized
In those cases, nanoscale analysis of wall ultrastructure would be required to firmly exclude a biological origin.

canonical_record.label: Nutrient limitation conditions basalt microbial element release
canonical_record.summary: In laboratory incubations of HSDP2 drill-core basalt with Burkholderia fungorum, release of Fe and other major elements exceeded abiotic controls only for nutrient-depleted rock-sample assays.

sources.title: Experimental Microbial Alteration and Fe Mobilization From Basaltic Rocks of the ICDP HSDP2 Drill Core, Hilo, Hawaii

statement: In laboratory incubations of HSDP2 drill-core basalt with Burkholderia fungorum, release of Fe and other major elements exceeded abiotic controls only for nutrient-depleted rock-sample assays.

scope.population: HSDP2 Hawaiian drill-core basalt incubated with one species, B. fungorum, compared to abiotic controls
scope.assumptions: Batch incubation with added glucose, prescribed growth medium and abiotic comparisons
scope.uncertainty: Assay-specific and conditioned on nutrient depletion; not a field-wide or seawater claim
scope.quantifiers: Exceeded controls only when the rock sample assay was nutrient depleted

support.quote: In biotic incubation experiments bacterial growth was observed and the release of Fe and other major elements from drill core basaltic rocks to solution exceeded that of abiotic controls only when the rock sample assay was nutrient depleted.

canonical_record.label: Synthetic basalt glass stress and Fe(II) track element release
canonical_record.summary: In biotic laboratory colonization assays using synthetic basaltic glasses, dissolved major-element concentrations increased with greater residual stress and Fe(II) content.

sources.title: Experimental Microbial Alteration and Fe Mobilization From Basaltic Rocks of the ICDP HSDP2 Drill Core, Hilo, Hawaii

statement: In biotic laboratory colonization assays using synthetic basaltic glasses, dissolved major-element concentrations increased with greater residual stress and Fe(II) content.

scope.population: Synthetic basaltic glasses of differing Fe oxidation states and residual stress exposed to B. fungorum in laboratory colonization assays
scope.assumptions: Assays varied Fe redox state and glass residual stress
scope.uncertainty: Reported correlation in tested glasses; factors are varied together in this summary and cannot be treated as separately isolated universal effects
scope.quantifiers: Increase across tested residual stress and Fe(II) conditions

support.quote: Additionally, colonization experiments with synthetic basaltic glasses of different Fe redox states and residual stresses were performed to evaluate their influence on microbial activity and surface attachment of cells.
The concentration of dissolved major elements in solution in biotic colonization experiments with synthetic basaltic glasses increased with increasing residual stress and Fe(II) content.

canonical_record.label: Biofilm coverage differs across synthetic basalt glass types
canonical_record.summary: The 2018 colonization assays reported dense biofilm on stressed Fe(II)-rich basalt glasses, versus sparse colonization on unstressed Fe(III)-rich glasses.

sources.title: Experimental Microbial Alteration and Fe Mobilization From Basaltic Rocks of the ICDP HSDP2 Drill Core, Hilo, Hawaii

statement: The 2018 colonization assays reported dense biofilm on stressed Fe(II)-rich basalt glasses, versus sparse colonization on unstressed Fe(III)-rich glasses.

scope.population: Synthetic basaltic glasses with contrasted residual-stress and Fe redox conditions in B. fungorum colonization experiments
scope.assumptions: Comparison of stressed Fe(II)-rich and unstressed Fe(III)-rich glass surfaces
scope.uncertainty: Joint contrast does not individually isolate stress or Fe oxidation state as sole cause
scope.quantifiers: Dense coverage in the first tested glass condition; sparse in the contrasted glass condition

support.quote: In colonization experiments, basaltic glasses with residual stress and high Fe(II) content were intensely covered with a cellular biofilm. In contrast, glasses with high Fe(III) content and no residual stress were sparsely colonized.
